purpose: Implementation plan for the Rust daemon (flow-core + flow-daemon + flow-platform) that will eventually sit behind docs/contracts/daemon-ipc.md, replacing flutter/lib/data/mock_daemon_repository.dart with a real process the Flutter UI talks to over local IPC. Mirrors the granularity and commit-per-task discipline of the root todos.json (Flutter phase). Every task embeds the spec excerpt it's built from (vision.md section or docs/contracts/*.md) so context survives a fresh session picking up a single task cold.

namingConventions.crates: flow-core (lib, no OS/transport/UI deps), flow-daemon (bin, wires everything together), flow-platform (per-OS adapters behind flow-core traits)
namingConventions.modules: snake_case matching existing core/src/{device,input,pairing,protocol,state,transport}/mod.rs layout; new modules follow the same one-concept-per-module rule
namingConventions.types: UpperCamelCase matching data-model.md's Dart types 1:1 (Device, DeviceState, DaemonLinkState, PairingSession, FlowSettings, SwitchKeyBinding, PermissionStatus) so a reviewer can diff Rust struct fields against the Dart class directly
namingConventions.wire_format: #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] on every contract type — Rust field foo_bar serializes as foo_bar, matching data-model.md's stated 'snake_case on the wire' rule without a translation layer
namingConventions.errors: thiserror-derived FlowError in flow_core::error, one variant per docs/contracts/daemon-ipc.md error code, Display message matching the code's human-readable meaning
namingConventions.async_runtime: tokio (rt-multi-thread) everywhere a daemon binary runs; flow-core stays runtime-agnostic (plain traits/types only, no tokio dependency) so platform adapters and tests aren't forced onto tokio

sharedContractConstants.ipcTransport: WebSocket over loopback TCP (127.0.0.1 only), chosen over Unix domain socket / named pipe so v0.1 needs exactly one implementation across macOS/Windows/Linux instead of #[cfg(target_os)] branching in the IPC layer itself. Revisit socket-based transport in track I as a hardening step once the contract is proven (README's data-model.md ground rule 3: this is local-only, assumed reachable only by the local user).
sharedContractConstants.mockParitySeedData: 3 devices: d1 'MacBook' (macos, active, local/unremovable), d2 'Work Laptop' (windows, inactive), d3 'Desktop' (linux, disconnected). 2 pairing candidates on start_pairing: 'Office Mac Mini' (macos), 'Studio Linux' (linux). Source: flutter/lib/data/mock_daemon_repository.dart.

mockParityTimings.note: daemon-ipc.md explicitly says these are NOT part of the contract for a real daemon (real latency depends on network + human accept/reject) — the mock-parity service (track B) matches them anyway so swapping the Flutter provider from mock to real-daemon-over-IPC is visually seamless during development, not because a real daemon must hit these numbers in production.

persistenceModel.library: rusqlite (bundled feature — statically-linked SQLite, no system libsqlite3 dependency needed on the macOS/Windows cross-compile targets) + rusqlite_migration for versioned schema
persistenceModel.concurrencyModel: single Connection wrapped in Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<_>>, every query run inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking since rusqlite is synchronous
persistenceModel.dbFile: one SQLite file under the platform data dir (via the directories crate); tests always use Connection::open_in_memory(), never the real filesystem

tables.settings: single row, one column per FlowSettings field, switch_key as label + JSON token array
tables.devices: paired devices — id/name/os/last_seen/public_key/removable. Doubles as the trust store: a device's public_key column IS its trust record, no separate trust file. DeviceState is never a column — always runtime-derived, starting Disconnected on load until a live connection re-establishes it.
tables.connection_history: append-only event log (device_id, event_type, occurred_at, detail), populated by observing the DaemonService watch-channel event bus (track P5) rather than by instrumenting every command handler
tables.identity: single row, this daemon's own ed25519 keypair (public_key, private_key), generated once and reused across restarts

persistenceModel.origin: User requirement: 'We'll need to maintain the user settings somewhere and maintain the connection history and things like that somewhere instead of deriving every run or keeping in memory.' Track P (persistence-storage) implements this and sits right after core-contract-parity — settings/device persistence is foundational to the very first working DaemonService (B1), not a late reliability-track afterthought as originally drafted.

wrapThirdPartyDependencies.rule: Every third-party crate that does real I/O or platform work sits behind a project-owned trait or type; application code (service logic, command handlers, the pipeline) depends only on the internal abstraction, never on the crate directly. This is the open/closed principle applied at the crate-boundary level: swapping rusqlite for another SQLite binding, or adding a second Bluetooth backend, should touch exactly one module.
wrapThirdPartyDependencies.origin: User requirement (verbatim): 'Make sure we always wrap third party dependencies into such abstract wrappers for better control over the application and open closed principles.'

examples.callersSeeOnly: the Channel trait — NoiseChannel itself wraps another Channel, it doesn't replace the abstraction

wrapThirdPartyDependencies.enforcement: Each task above that introduces a new third-party crate says explicitly, in its own acceptanceCriteria, that the crate's usage is confined to one module (checkable with a grep for the crate's import path outside that module). This is spot-checked per task, not left as an aspirational rule — see G2/G4/H3 for the pattern.

channels.summary: The daemon-to-daemon communication abstraction, named 'Channels' per explicit product naming. A Channel is established between two devices over TCP (Wi-Fi/local network) or Bluetooth, whichever is available — see track G and docs/architecture/channels.md for the full design.
channels.documentedIn: docs/architecture/channels.md — maintained separately from docs/contracts/ (that directory is exclusively the Flutter<->daemon local IPC contract; Channels is daemon<->daemon, a different boundary, per docs/contracts/README.md ground rule 3), but written in the same style/discipline (versioned, wire examples, explicit out-of-scope section) so the two stay easy to reconcile if Channel state ever needs to surface into the Flutter-facing contract (e.g. a future 'connection medium' field on Device).

tasks.title: Connection history logger
tasks.buildNote: Split into two files rather than the single history_logger.rs the deliverables text named: daemon/src/storage/connection_history_repo.rs (ConnectionHistoryRepo — matching the established one-repo-per-file pattern from P3/P4/P6) and daemon/src/storage/history_logger.rs (just the spawned observer task). Extracted the RFC3339 parse helper device_repo.rs already had into storage::parse_rfc3339 (pub(crate)) and reused it from both device_repo and connection_history_repo instead of duplicating it, per the 'check if you can reuse before writing a new method' instruction. spawn() takes &DaemonService + Storage and returns a JoinHandle, to be held by main.rs in C4 alongside the IPC listener/hotkey runner as the task's deliverable line specifies. Device-diff logging only logs a device becoming Active (not one becoming Inactive) and only logs removals (not additions) so a switch produces exactly one row and a pairing produces exactly one row from the pairing_session arm, not a duplicate from the devices arm — verified directly by the two named acceptance-criteria tests. The pairing_session arm peeks devices_rx.borrow() fresh (not the loop's own last_devices) to resolve target_name to a device id, avoiding a real race where tokio::select! could service the pairing branch before the devices branch despite both watch values already being committed. link_state_changed logging is implemented (schema-compatible NON_DEVICE_EVENT_ID sentinel 'daemon' for the NOT NULL device_id column, since a link-state transition isn't about one device) but has no test — DaemonLinkState is set once at construction and no command in tracks A-B currently mutates it, so this arm is presently unreachable; it will become exercisable once a later track (I - reliability-persistence) starts changing link_state. tasks.title: Pairing commands and async state-machine timers
tasks.buildNote: DaemonService now derives Clone (all fields are Arc/Storage/watch::Sender, all cheaply Clone) so timer callbacks can hold their own owned handle instead of borrowing self across .await/tokio::spawn. Key-name comparison (both `held` and the checked token) is case-insensitive via to_ascii_uppercase(), since the token vocabulary (data-model.md's presets, e.g. "ScrollLock") and each platform's own key_name() output (e.g. Linux's evdev-derived "SCROLLLOCK") were designed independently in separate tracks and never shared a casing convention - discovered while writing this task's own tests, not assumed. tracks.title: channels
tracks.goal: Real daemon-to-daemon connectivity through a single custom abstraction — a Channel — that can be backed by TCP (Wi-Fi/local network) or Bluetooth depending on what's available between two devices, so the rest of the daemon (pairing, input streaming, security) never talks to a concrete transport crate directly. Documented separately in docs/architecture/channels.md, kept consistent in vocabulary with docs/contracts but explicitly not part of that contract (it's daemon-to-daemon, not Flutter-to-daemon).

tasks.description: New core/src/channel/mod.rs defining the Channel trait and its vocabulary, replacing the placeholder core::transport::Transport (fold it in here rather than keeping two overlapping abstractions). tasks.buildNote: Chose the plan's explicitly-sanctioned UDP-broadcast fallback over mdns-sd, and verified why directly rather than guessing: a manual test of a genuine SO_BROADCAST send to 255.255.255.255 in this sandboxed container came back with the packet's source address rewritten to a 192.0.2.x (TEST-NET-1) address by some NAT/proxy layer - real broadcast delivery here is not something to build an automated test around, and mDNS multicast would face the same or worse restriction. daemon/src/discovery/tcp.rs: DiscoveryService::bind(listen_port, name, os, channel_port) binds 0.0.0.0 with SO_BROADCAST set (correct for real deployment - receives broadcasts arriving on any interface); announce_to(destination) sends one JSON Announce{name, os, channel_port} packet (channel_port is the peer's own TcpChannel listener port, separate from the fixed DISCOVERY_PORT=47824 every daemon's discovery listener binds); recv_one() parses one incoming packet, pairing the sender's actual IP (not something the packet claims) with the advertised channel_port into a ChannelAddress::Tcp - and returns Ok(None) rather than an error for anything that isn't valid JSON, since this UDP port can receive arbitrary non-Flow traffic; spawn_listener() forwards a stream of successfully-parsed DiscoveredPeers on an mpsc channel. tasks.title: Encrypted Channel decorator
tasks.buildNote: daemon/src/channel/noise.rs: NoiseChannel<C: Channel> wraps any Channel with a Noise_XX_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s session (snow crate, confined to this module). Deliberate deviation from the task's literal 'keyed by each side's H1 identity' phrasing, documented extensively in the module doc comment, daemon/README.md, and docs/architecture/channels.md: H1's DeviceIdentity is an ed25519 signing key, Noise's XX pattern needs an X25519 DH key - different primitives; converting one into the other needs a birational-map conversion this codebase doesn't implement and shouldn't hand-roll for a security-critical path without a well-audited library. Instead, NoiseChannel generates a fresh per-connection X25519 keypair for the handshake itself, then binds the resulting session to each side's real H1 identity via a signed-transcript exchange: both sides sign the Noise handshake hash (get_handshake_hash(), unique per session, preventing replay across connections) with their H1 identity and exchange {public_key, signature} as the first message over the now-encrypted transport; the peer's proven identity is exposed via peer_identity(). Added ChannelMessage::Noise(Vec<u8>) to core/src/channel/mod.rs to carry handshake/transport frames (the inner Channel already frames whole messages, so no extra length-prefixing needed), and ChannelError::AuthenticationFailed for handshake/verification failures. Explicitly flagged as a reasonable, standard technique that has NOT been independently security-reviewed - this project's own best-effort implementation, not a substitute for professional cryptographic audit (documented honestly rather than implying production-grade security guarantees). 3 unit tests (full handshake + identity-proof verification, message round trip, kind() delegation) against real loopback TcpChannels. daemon/tests/noise_channel.rs is the acceptance-criteria integration test: a real TCP relay sniffs every byte between two TcpChannel endpoints and confirms a distinctive marker string never appears when sent through a NoiseChannel, plus a negative-control test proving the same marker DOES appear over a plain (unencrypted) TcpChannel - validating the sniff methodology itself, not just asserting a tautology. That control had to send server->client rather than client->server: RFC 6455 requires every client-to-server WebSocket frame to be XOR-masked, which would hide the marker from a literal byte search regardless of encryption - a real gotcha caught by writing the control test, not assumed. Second acceptance criterion (no TcpChannel/BluetoothChannel reference in NoiseChannel's own code) verified via grep: the only matches are in a doc comment and the #[cfg(test)] module, matching the same test-needs-a-concrete-type pattern G2/G4/G6/G7's own tests already establish. cargo build/test/clippy clean both with and without --features bluetooth; cargo fmt clean; full workspace test suite green (85 daemon lib tests without bluetooth / 91 with, plus the 2 new noise_channel integration tests).
tasks.description: NoiseChannel: a struct implementing Channel that wraps any other Box<dyn Channel> (Noise operates over any ordered byte stream, so this works identically over TcpChannel or, once G4 lands, BluetoothChannel — the whole reason G1's abstraction exists is so this task doesn't care which one it's wrapping) and layers an authenticated Noise protocol (snow crate) handshake keyed by each side's H1 identity, so ChannelMessages never travel in plaintext between daemons.
deliverables: snow added as a dependency, confined to this module per the wrap-third-party-deps rule
daemon/src/channel/noise.rs: struct NoiseChannel<C: Channel> implementing Channel, performing the handshake on construction and encrypting/decrypting every send/recv

tasks.buildNote: daemon/src/channel/reconnect.rs: maintain_connection(addresses, settings: watch::Receiver<FlowSettings>, link_state: watch::Sender<DaemonLinkState>, handle_connection) establishes a Channel via G6's connect_best_available, hands it to the caller-supplied handle_connection closure (which owns the connection's send/recv loop and returns when it ends), and re-negotiates from scratch on every retry rather than remembering the last medium - matching docs/architecture/channels.md's own stated auto-reconnect design note (already written by an earlier session, this task just implements it).
